persona.bio: Owns a small women's clothing boutique, just her and two part timers. Working the floor, buying at markets twice a year, posting new arrivals on Instagram, steaming and tagging stock, window displays every month, payroll and paying vendors, answering DMs about sizes and holds. She does most of it on her iPhone between customers. Instagram and the DMs take the most time, then tagging stock. She uses ChatGPT some weeks for captions and Canva's AI for posts.

path.role: You own a small women’s clothing boutique with two part timers, and you handle the social posts, restocking, customer texts, scheduling and the rest yourself, mostly from your phone.

steps.note: I own a small women’s clothing boutique with two part timers. I write to shoppers and regulars on Instagram, by text and by email. I like a warm, friendly voice that sounds like a real person, short and easy to read, with plain words. Keep posts to a few lines and replies to a couple of sentences. Never add details I did not give you, like prices, sizes, colors, sale dates or store hours. If something is missing, put it in square brackets for me to fill in. Never promise that an item will be in stock. Give me a draft I can read and change before anything goes out.

steps.title: Your Instagram posts, written with AI
steps.read: From now on, you open ChatGPT when a post is due, tell it what just came in, and it drafts the post in your voice. You stop copying an old post and changing a few words. Each post fits what you are really selling that week, and you read it before it goes up.

material.label: Your post request
items: Write an Instagram post for my women’s clothing boutique. Today’s news: [what arrived or what is on sale]. Details I want in it: [colors, sizes, anything shoppers must know]. Keep my voice: warm, friendly and short, like this one I wrote before: “New arrivals just in! Linen wrap dresses in sage and rust, sizes XS to XL. Tap the link in bio to shop. DM us to hold one before it sells out.” Use only the details I gave you and add nothing else. Give me three versions, each under [number] words, with a call to action at the end, so I can pick one and change it.

steps.title: Your customer messages, saved once on your phone
steps.read: Your common replies live on your phone’s keyboard, each a few letters away. When a message comes in, you type the shortcut, tap the reply and change the name or time. Your answers stay consistent and you stop typing the same thing again and again.

material.label: Your replies
items: Hi [first name]! Thanks so much for reaching out. Yes, we have that in stock right now. Want me to hold it for you?
Hi [first name]! That one is sold out at the moment. I can let you know when it comes back in. Want me to?
Sure thing, I can hold it for you until [day and time]. Just stop by before then and ask for me.
We have [sizes] in that style. Come try it on any time, or tell me what size you usually wear and I can help you pick.
Our hours are [store hours]. We would love to see you!
Thank you for shopping with us, [first name]! If anything is not quite right, let me know and we will sort it out together.
Hi [first name]! New pieces just came in that I think you will love. Want me to send you photos?

safeUse: Never type a customer’s full name, phone number, home address or payment details into ChatGPT. Use square brackets instead.
Keep your sales numbers, supplier prices and part timers’ personal details out of the chat.
Read every post and reply before it goes out, and check sizes, colors, prices and hours yourself.
Only promise what you know is true, like what is in stock and what you can hold.
Never let it make up details about your clothes, your sales or your store policies.

design.today: You write social posts a few times a week, and each one starts as a copy of an old post. You check what sold well first, then work from your phone.
design.newWay: You keep one saved assistant in ChatGPT that knows your shop's voice and how your past posts read. When a new arrival comes in, you tell it what landed and what sold well, and it gives you a post draft in your style. You read it, fix any detail, and post it yourself, so you stop starting from an old post each time.

steps.goal: Get ChatGPT ready on your phone so you can use it where you already work.
Save a short note about your boutique and how you like to sound so every draft starts from it.
Pick three or four of your best past posts, including the linen wrap dress one, to show the assistant your style.
Build a saved assistant that turns the details of new stock into a post in your voice.
Post the draft you approved yourself, after adding the link and checking the details.

material.label: Shop voice notes
material.what: A short description of how your posts sound, including your call to action about the link in bio and holding items by DM.

material.label: Assistant instructions
material.what: Instructions for your saved assistant on turning stock details like item, colors and sizes into a post.

material.label: Example posts
material.what: A few of your own past posts the assistant copies the style from.

material.label: New arrival prompt
material.what: A short fill in the blanks message you paste in with the item, colors, sizes and what sold well lately.

design.checkPoint: You read each draft and check the item, colors, sizes and link before you post it yourself.

design.today: You answer customer messages by hand as they come in, one at a time. Most of it happens on your phone by text and chat.
design.newWay: You save your most common replies on your phone so each one is a few letters away. Questions that need a little more thought you can paste into your ChatGPT assistant for a draft. You still read and send every reply yourself, but you stop retyping the same answers.

steps.goal: List the ten questions customers ask you most, like holds, sizes, hours and restocks.
Get ChatGPT ready on your phone so it can help word the replies.
Turn your ten common answers into saved replies on your phone keyboard.
Save a short note about your shop and tone so drafts for odd questions sound like you.

material.label: Ten saved replies
material.what: Short ready answers to your most common customer questions, each with a short shortcut.

material.label: Tone notes
material.what: A few lines on how you talk to regulars, so longer drafts sound like you.

material.label: Shop facts sheet
material.what: Your hours, hold policy, return rules and sizing notes, written by you for the assistant to use.

design.checkPoint: You read every reply before you send it, and nothing is sent by itself.
